Lorentz-Hyperbolic Weighted Penalized Regression

lhwpr.Rd

Fit local Gaussian or binomial penalized regressions whose observation weights are defined by Lorentz-hyperbolic neighborhoods.

Usage

lhwpr(
  formula,
  data,
  Z,
  bw,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial"),
  penalty = c("lasso", "mcp", "scad"),
  alpha = 1,
  lambda = NULL,
  nlambda = 100L,
  lambda_min_ratio = NULL,
  gamma = NULL,
  penalty_factor = NULL,
  case_weights = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  kernel = hgwr_kernel_names(),
  adaptive = TRUE,
  bandwidth_type = c("knn", "volume"),
  geometry = c("lorentz", "tangent"),
  tangent_ref = NULL,
  dMat = NULL,
  engine = c("dense", "knn"),
  keep_path = c("auto", "all", "selected"),
  control = lhwpr_control()
)

# S3 method for class 'lhwpr'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lhwpr'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.lhwpr'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lhwpr'
coef(object, s = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lhwpr'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lhwpr'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lhwpr'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  Znew = NULL,
  type = c("response", "link", "coefficients"),
  s = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lhwpr'
plot(
  x,
  focus = 1L,
  xvar = c("lambda", "lambda_ratio"),
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

A model formula with one response and one or more predictors.

data

A data frame containing variables in formula.

Z

An n by 3 matrix of Lorentz-hyperboloid coordinates.

bw

Kernel bandwidth, or neighbor count for adaptive kNN fitting.

family

Gaussian or binomial response family.

penalty

Structural penalty: lasso, MCP, or SCAD. It is ignored when alpha = 0.

alpha

Mixing value in [0, 1]. Zero is ridge; a value strictly between zero and one is elastic net and requires the lasso penalty; one gives lasso, MCP, or SCAD.

lambda

Optional strictly decreasing common absolute lambda path.

nlambda

Number of automatically generated lambda values.

lambda_min_ratio

Ratio of the final to initial automatic lambda.

gamma

MCP or SCAD concavity parameter.

penalty_factor

Optional non-negative multiplier for each non-intercept coefficient.

case_weights

Optional non-negative case weights.

standardize

Whether predictors are centered and scaled once on the full analysis sample.

kernel

Lorentz-distance kernel.

adaptive

Whether bw is adaptive.

bandwidth_type

Neighbor-count or hyperbolic-volume bandwidth scale.

geometry

Intrinsic Lorentz or tangent-space distance geometry.

tangent_ref

Optional Lorentz point defining the tangent plane.

dMat

Optional precomputed distance matrix.

engine

Dense or exact compact-kernel kNN computation.

keep_path

Whether to retain all local coefficient paths.

control

A control object from lhwpr_control().

x, object

A fitted lhwpr object, or its summary.

s

A lambda value exactly represented in the fitted path.

newdata

Optional predictor data for new focal locations.

Znew

Lorentz coordinates corresponding to newdata.

type

Prediction scale or local coefficients.

focus

One-based focal-location index for a path plot.

xvar

Horizontal path scale.

...

Additional arguments passed to the plotting method.

Details

At every focal location, kernel and case weights are multiplied and normalized before fitting. Predictor standardization is global rather than focal. For a given bandwidth, every focal model uses the same absolute lambda values.

Lasso and elastic-net paths use warm starts, sequential strong screening, and a full KKT repair pass. MCP and SCAD use curvature-aware scalar minimization and full stationarity scans. Binomial models use proximal Newton/IRLS.

The intercept is never penalized. Group penalties are not part of LHWPR. Classical unpenalized LHWR inference is not attached to penalized fits.

With keep_path = "auto", a full dense coefficient cube is retained only when it contains at most ten million values. Selected coefficients and all fitted-value paths are retained regardless. Use keep_path = "all" to override this memory guard.

Value

lhwpr() returns an object of class "lhwpr" with selected local coefficients and predictions, lambda metadata, optional paths, convergence and KKT diagnostics, preprocessing metadata, and geometry information. Extractor methods return the corresponding component.

Examples

set.seed(1)
H <- simulate_H2(40, r_max = 2)
dat <- data.frame(
  y = rnorm(40),
  x1 = rnorm(40),
  x2 = rnorm(40)
)
fit <- lhwpr(
  y ~ x1 + x2,
  data = dat,
  Z = H$Z,
  bw = 15,
  alpha = 0.5,
  nlambda = 10
)
coef(fit)
